review_notes: Read the whole target file, Edge.lean's two existence lemmas, and grepped all uses in the repo. Four theorems here (continuousOn_schwarzChristoffelBoundary, schwarzChristoffelBoundary_sub_eq, schwarzChristoffelBoundary_injOn, collinear_schwarzChristoffelBoundary_image) repeat the same bridge: get L with pointwise limits from an Edge lemma, then rewrite the boundary map to L with schwarzChristoffelBoundary_eq_of_tendsto. The repetition is small per site, so this is a modest finding. I found no other substantial repeated arguments. The exponent-sum-zero argument in sum_filter_eq_zero_of_mem_Ioo is used once. I did not check whether the proposed helper compiles.

findings.problem: Four theorems on a prevertex-free interval share one bridge. Each obtains an auxiliary L from an Edge lemma (`exists_tendsto_schwarzChristoffelPrimitive_sub_eq` or `..._injOn_collinear`). Each then converts L's pointwise limit property into an equality `schwarzChristoffelBoundary a e z₀ x = L x` via `schwarzChristoffelBoundary_eq_of_tendsto`, re-doing the conversion at x and y or via a hand-written `ext`/`rintro` set-image argument. The Edge lemmas bundle the facts about L with an unconstrained L, so every consumer has to transfer them to the boundary map by hand. `collinear_schwarzChristoffelBoundary_image` spends about ten lines on this, using `convert` and a two-direction `ext`. The same `obtain` plus limit-to-equality step also appears in Infinity/Basic.lean, with `limUnder_eq`.
findings.proposed_change: Add one private (or public) lemma stating that on `Ioo p q` the boundary map has the same limit data as the Edge lemmas. A simple form is `∀ x ∈ Ioo p q, Tendsto (schwarzChristoffelPrimitive a e z₀) (𝓝[upperHalfPlaneSet] (x:ℂ)) (𝓝 (schwarzChristoffelBoundary a e z₀ x))`. This follows from `tendsto_schwarzChristoffelPrimitive_boundary` with the exponent sum `0 > -1` given by `sum_filter_eq_zero_of_mem_Ioo`. A stronger form is `∃ L, EqOn (schwarzChristoffelBoundary a e z₀) L (Ioo p q) ∧ <the Edge conclusions about L>`. Then `injOn`, `collinear` and `continuousOn` follow from `EqOn.injOn_iff`, `Set.image_congr` and `ContinuousOn.congr`, with no manual `ext`. `sub_eq` becomes a rewrite with `EqOn`. A simpler alternative is to restate the Edge lemmas directly for the boundary map and drop the existential L.
findings.benefit: The limit-to-equality step is proved once and each call site becomes a short transfer through EqOn or Set.image_congr. The `collinear` proof loses its manual two-direction `ext`. Future edge results on the boundary map will not need to re-open the `∃ L` statements.
